description: Count the distinct orders with risk/margin records for each order type. For the types above the average count, return the average of their counts and their average excess over that average.

c.request: Matching risk/margin records to their orders (`ordervault` = `recordvault`) and ignoring unmatched ones, how many risk/margin-matched orders does each order type (`ordertune`) have? For the types above the average count across types, give one row with the average of their counts and the average amount by which they exceed that average, without rounding. Count the distinct orders with risk/margin records for each order type. For the types above the average count, return the average of their counts and their average excess over that average.
c.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM orders AS o JOIN riskandmargin AS r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), overall AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count FROM type_counts) SELECT AVG(t.order_count) AS average_count, AVG(t.order_count - o.average_count) AS average_excess FROM type_counts AS t CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE t.order_count > o.average_count

b.request: For each order type, count distinct orders matched to at least one risk/margin record; among types whose count exceeds the average count across all order types, return one row containing the unrounded average of their counts and the unrounded average amount by which their counts exceed that overall average
b.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.riskandmarginpivot IS NOT NULL THEN o.orderspivot END) AS order_count FROM orders AS o LEFT JOIN riskandmargin AS r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), compared AS (SELECT order_count, AVG(order_count) OVER () AS overall_avg FROM type_counts) SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_order_count, AVG(order_count - overall_avg) AS avg_excess_count FROM compared WHERE order_count > overall_avg

a.request: Matching risk/margin records to orders (`ordervault` = `recordvault`) and dropping those without a match, count the distinct orders for each order type (`ordertune`), so an order with two risk/margin records counts once. Then, for the types whose count is above the average count across types, give one row with the average of their counts and the average amount by which their counts exceed that average, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH counts_by_type AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), overall AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count FROM counts_by_type) SELECT AVG(c.order_count) AS avg_above_average_count, AVG(c.order_count - a.avg_count) AS avg_excess_count FROM counts_by_type AS c CROSS JOIN overall AS a WHERE c.order_count > a.avg_count

d.request: Match risk/margin records to orders where `ordervault = recordvault`, ignoring unmatched records. Count the distinct matched orders for each order type (`ordertune`). For order types whose counts exceed the average count across all types, return one row containing the average of their counts and their average excess over the overall average, without rounding.
d.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), counts_with_average AS (SELECT order_count, AVG(order_count) OVER () AS overall_average FROM type_counts) SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count, AVG(order_count - overall_average) AS average_excess FROM counts_with_average WHERE order_count > overall_average
